235K likes, 1,916 comments - rajshamani on February 25, 2024: "MY DREAM CONCERT 🤫

Who said in India people only pay for music concerts and entertainment?

Look at the biggest convention center of the country jam packed with thousands of people, who are there for growth.

India is changing and India wants to grow🫡 

Post 1: Look at the face of this kid on the stage who is living a dream he saw at the age of 19 with no money, no influence and no fancy degree, to deliver a speech in front of fully sold out stadium. 🫣

Post 2: My parents saw me live at a conference for the first time, this proud look on their face is the reason why I am happy crying rn❤️

Post 3: Me looking at all of you, and thanking every god in the world. What have I done right to deserve an audience like yours? 🤍🥺

Post 4: right before my speech dad came backstage to hug me and wish me good luck. (Ofcourse after this jhappi the speech had to be good) 🙇🏻‍♂️

Post 5: Hi! I am Raj Shamani. (please read it like: Yeh sheher mera hai and mei is shehar ka Bajirao Singham)

Post 6: Ofcourse I had to talk about: ‘THREE THINGS’ 😂

Post 7 & 8: Just in my element.

Post 9: My family post speech looks complete, my younger brother, dad & mom along with @rajivtalreja  who’s the big brother I never had who ran to me back stage after the speech to come and validate me that it went well. 🤍 (Later whatsapped me 3 things that I need to improve from next time, because ofcourse he is is the one who is never completely satisfied with my speeches because he wants me to reach the next level) 

Post 10: Stage for me is a holy place, where for me nothing matters apart from ‘how to give maximum value to my audience’, and how to serve people who are giving me the most important time of their lives. ✨".

267K likes, 2,873 comments - rajshamani on January 30, 2023: "At age 16, I used to go to English classes to learn how to speak English fluently and while sitting in the tuition centre I used to write random dreams at the back of my notebook. 😂 

I had no talent, no background, was not from a big city, did not have good grades to make it to IIT / IIM, and wasn’t even able to speak in English properly but I used to believe that I had ‘shaka-laka boom boom magic) 😂 

29th July 2013 - I wrote in my dairy that I will be on the cover of Forbes magazine, (I and my sisters laughed at this crazy dream)

Age 26 - I made it to Forbes cover and Forbes 30 under 30.😭😭

And at this moment, the teenager in me is screaming at the top of his lungs that 'we made it.'

And today, the big dream has finally hit this boy from a small city -Indore.

This would have never been possible without your love and belief in me.

Truth be told, I started my entrepreneurship journey when I was 16 solely because I wanted to achieve this🤫

But along the line, I have fallen in love with the process of educating and helping 100s and 1000s of people.🥺

Coming from a humble family and city, having big dreams was considered a 'luxury.' But today as I get acknowledged for fulfilling mine, it isn't just me who wins.

This is a win for everyone who doubts themselves for not being talented enough, 
not being rich enough, not being from the big city, not being an IIM/IIT graduate & still continue to believe in their dreams. 

it’s a win for all of them, all of us.❤️

Now that we have this baby home, I am ready to go back to basics and fulfil my duty of building the nation, one day at a time.

P.S. Thank you all from the deepest corner of my heart, each of you that has supported me has a special place in my heart. 😭

- Picture 3 is where I wrote 10 years ago about my dream of a Forbes cover when I didn’t even know what a startup was. 

- Picture 4 is my notes from ‘basic English classes, I took’ 

- Picture 5 is the back of my diary where I used to write random dreams like ‘start a business, ‘give a speech at IIM’ and ‘It is possible to interview people’ 😂

THIS IS YOUR SIGN AND PROOF, THAT DREAMS DO COME TRUE, DON’T LET ANYONE TELL YOU ANYTHING ELSE🥺".

46K likes, 112 comments - rajshamani on October 9, 2026: "Sometimes, the biggest thing holding you back isn’t your talent, your circumstances, or the opportunities you get. It’s the identity you’ve built around yourself.

If you believe you’re someone who always gives up when things get difficult, you’ll find reasons to quit. If you believe you’re someone who isn’t good enough, you’ll hesitate even when an opportunity is right in front of you. And if you’ve convinced yourself that a certain level of success is all you deserve, you might unconsciously stop yourself from going beyond it.

Not because you lack the ability, but because your actions are constantly trying to stay consistent with the person you believe you are.

That’s why real growth begins when you stop asking, “Am I capable of doing this?” and start asking, “Who do I need to become to make this happen?”

You don’t become confident and then take action. Sometimes, you take action while you’re scared, and that’s how confidence develops.

You don’t become disciplined overnight. You build discipline every time you keep a promise to yourself, especially when nobody is watching.

And you don’t become successful by waiting until you feel like a successful person. You become one by making the decisions, accepting the discomfort, and doing the work that your future self would be proud of.

Your current identity is often built from your past experiences, failures, fears, and the opinions you’ve accepted about yourself. But your past is evidence of what you’ve experienced, not a limit on what you can become.

So, stop using your current version as proof of your future potential.

You are allowed to outgrow the person you’ve been. You’re allowed to change your standards, challenge your old beliefs, and become someone your past self wouldn’t even recognise.

Your potential is not the problem. The way you see yourself might be.

Start becoming the person who can handle the life you keep dreaming about.".

15K likes, 84 comments - figuringout.co on October 8, 2026: "Comment ‘AI’ and we’ll personally DM you the full conversation.

Would you rather build something people don’t understand today or something everyone already wants?

In today’s episode, we sit down with Sravanth Aluru (@alurusravanth) CEO & Co-founder of Avataar.ai an IIT Bombay and Wharton alum who left Wall Street tech banking to bet on AI, and whose team built Varya under the IndiaAI Mission.

Here’s what we discussed:
-The Two Games Every Founder Must Choose From: Why founders need to decide whether they are playing a short-term or long-term game.
-Why Your Idea Should Sound Stupid: Why ideas that seem unusual or crazy at first can sometimes create the biggest opportunities.
-Why Companies Should Rethink AI Tools: The risks and challenges of allowing employees to use AI without proper systems or safeguards.
-Why Coders Could Be Among the First Jobs Disrupted by AI: How rapidly improving AI capabilities are changing software development and the future of technical jobs.
-Why Being Early Can Be Your Biggest Advantage: Why building five years ahead of the market can be more valuable than arriving when everyone else is already there.

Catch the full episode here:
YouTube Channel: Raj Shamani
Spotify Channel: Raj Shamani Figuring Out

Until then, keep figuring out! 🚀

#rajshamani #figuringout".

62K likes, 136 comments - rajshamani on October 8, 2026: "You keep saying you’ll start tomorrow.
You’ll wake up early.
You’ll get serious.
You’ll stop wasting time.

And every time you don’t, you make another excuse.

Eventually, you stop feeling guilty. You just lower your standards and accept it as who you are.

That’s when life gets dangerous.

Because the real damage isn’t one bad day. It’s slowly losing trust in yourself.

You don’t need to change your entire life overnight.

Start by keeping one promise to yourself.

Do what you said you would do.

Because every promise you keep rebuilds self-respect.

And sometimes, getting your life back starts with simply becoming someone you can trust again.".

What is one memory from your childhood that you still remember vividly?

In today’s episode, we sit down with Nikolay Kukushkin (@niko_kukushkin) Neuroscientist & 
Author, One Hand Clapping a memory scientist who calls himself a “molecular philosopher” and studies how molecules and cells create memory, motivation and consciousness.

Here’s what we discussed:
-Why Your Brain Rewrites Memories: How recalling a memory can actually change the way you remember it.
-Can Talking About Trauma Make It Stronger?: Why repeatedly revisiting certain memories may affect how strongly they stay with you.
-The Man Who Remembered Everything: What extreme memory can teach us about the way our brains process and store experiences.
-Why Dopamine Is About Wanting: Why dopamine is more connected to motivation and pursuit than simply feeling pleasure.
-Why You’re Never Fully Satisfied: How evolution shaped our brains to keep wanting more, even after achieving what we wanted.

Catch the full episode here:
YouTube Channel: Raj Shamani
Spotify Channel: Raj Shamani Figuring Out

Until then, keep figuring out! 🚀

#rajshamani #figuringout".

57K likes, 153 comments - rajshamani on October 6, 2026: "Sometimes, the easiest decision today becomes the hardest life tomorrow.

You avoid the difficult conversation because it feels uncomfortable.
You stay in a job you’ve outgrown because starting over feels scary.
You keep delaying the work because scrolling feels easier.
You spend instead of saving because enjoying the money feels better right now.
You choose comfort over discipline because discipline demands something from you.

And none of these decisions feel dangerous in the moment.

That’s the trap.

Emotional comfort gives you instant relief, but sometimes sends the bill to your future self.

The work you avoid today becomes the pressure you carry tomorrow.
The money you waste today becomes the financial stress you face later.
The boundaries you refuse to set today become resentment tomorrow.
The risks you keep avoiding can slowly turn into regret.

Growing up is realising that not everything that feels good is good for you, and not everything that feels difficult is bad for you.

Sometimes, the uncomfortable choice is actually the kindest thing you can do for your future self.

Choose the harder conversation.
Choose the uncomfortable discipline.
Choose to save.
Choose to learn.
Choose to walk away when you know something is no longer right.

Because your future is being shaped by the things you keep choosing today.".
